name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: Learn by doing: a Wisconsin college trains data centre technicians with Microsoft, VS Code lets agents check each other's work, and Teams' Facilitator is due to turn meetings into slides.
window: Window: the 24 hours to 05:23 AEDT, Thu 5 Nov 2026 (Wednesday 4 Nov in the US).
notes: Reported: Datacenter Academy figures (14 certificates and 206 enrolled by the end of May; $2,277 tuition and about $760 for books) come from Gateway Technical College's dean via the Hechinger Report.

Facilitator's PowerPoint decks are a roadmap feature in development, due December 2026. VS Code's mixed harnesses are in preview and Blobby is experimental; the MCP gateway, Storage Discovery insights and Azure SQL backup locks are in public preview.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 5 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

stories.title: A Wisconsin college trains data centre technicians in a Microsoft Datacenter Academy
stories.summary: Gateway Technical College's Microsoft Datacenter Academy offers four hands-on courses over two semesters toward a Microsoft Data Center Certificate. By the end of May, 14 students had reportedly earned it and 206 were enrolled, and Microsoft-funded scholarships cover the $2,277 tuition and about $760 for books.

stories.title: VS Code 1.145 lets Claude review a plan Copilot wrote, and adds a Blobby break game
stories.summary: In Visual Studio Code 1.145, nested agent sessions can use different harnesses side by side (a preview setting), so you can ask Claude to review a plan a Copilot chat wrote, or give Codex the same task. It also adds cron schedules for local automations and an experimental Blobby jump game for short breaks.

stories.title: Teams' Facilitator is due to turn meeting discussions into PowerPoint decks
stories.summary: You'll be able to ask Facilitator to create a PowerPoint presentation from what was said, the chat and the shared files in a Teams meeting; it can already draft documents in Word. Handy, for example, after a staff meeting. It's in development on the Microsoft 365 roadmap for December.

stories.title: Azure Application Gateway for Containers can now front MCP servers, in preview
stories.summary: A new MCPRoute resource lets platform teams publish MCP servers for AI agents behind a stable hostname and path, with TLS, JWT validation and the web application firewall managed centrally. JWT validation and private ingress also reached public preview the same day.

stories.title: Azure Site Recovery's improved disaster recovery for flexible scale sets is generally available
stories.summary: Azure Site Recovery now offers an enhanced disaster recovery experience for virtual machines in Virtual Machine Scale Sets with flexible orchestration, with better target configuration and end-to-end failover and reprotect.

stories.title: Azure Storage Discovery now shows access patterns, data age and tiers, in preview
stories.summary: Advanced capacity insights in Azure Storage Discovery give more visibility into storage use, including access patterns, data age, storage tiers, object size distribution and retention, so teams can see which data is old or rarely touched.

stories.title: Azure SQL backups can stay immutable for the full retention period, in preview
stories.summary: Azure SQL Database and SQL Managed Instance can now lock point-in-time restore backups as immutable for the whole configured retention, beyond the default 7 days of immutable backups that were already available.

stories.title: Application Insights API keys for queries now retire on 31 March 2027
stories.summary: Microsoft has extended the retirement date: on 31 March 2027, API keys used to query Azure Monitor Application Insights data will be retired, so apps and scripts that use them need to switch to Microsoft Entra ID.

stories.title: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School is on Game Pass from 5 November
stories.summary: The sequel joins its timed escape rooms into an explorable, puzzle-filled campus, solo or in local or online co-op, on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox on PC and day one with Game Pass. Xbox Wire's tips: keep a pencil and paper handy and think backwards from the goal.

stories.title: Xbox's Nano Controller is out at $49.99, built for smaller hands
stories.summary: The new controller measures 133 x 66.5 x 36.6 mm and weighs 101 g, about a third of a standard Xbox Wireless Controller, with a built-in battery that charges over USB-C. It works with Xbox consoles, Windows PCs, tablets, compatible smart TVs and iOS or Android devices; $49.99 is the US price.

transcript.t: This is the Microsoft for Education Daily, for Thursday.
Let's catch you up on everything new from Microsoft.
Learn by doing. At a Wisconsin college, a Microsoft Datacenter Academy trains data centre technicians.
By May, 14 had the certificate, and 206 were enrolled.
Microsoft-funded scholarships cover the tuition, about $2,300, and the books.
Gateway's dean says it isn't really about steering graduates to Microsoft.
It's for the whole community.
Student coders? In VS Code, Claude can review a plan Copilot wrote, in preview.
And when you need a break, there's Blobby, a little jumping game starring the VS Code pet.
Staff meeting? In December, Teams' Facilitator is due to turn what was said into a PowerPoint deck.
It works from the conversation, the meeting chat and shared files. It already drafts in Word.
University IT building AI agents?
Azure can now put MCP servers behind one gateway, in preview.
And Azure Site Recovery's improved disaster recovery for flexible scale sets is now generally available.
Research storage piling up? Azure Storage Discovery now shows access patterns, data age and tiers, in preview.
So you can see which data is old or rarely touched, and how much sits in each tier.
The fine print? In preview, Azure SQL backups can stay locked for the full retention, not just seven days.
And Application Insights API keys now retire on March 31, 2027. Switch to Entra.
After hours? Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School is on Game Pass from November 5.
Xbox's tips? Keep a pencil and paper handy, and think backwards from the goal.
And Xbox's new Nano Controller is out: 101 grams, built for smaller hands.
Hands-on courses, agents checking agents, pencil-and-paper puzzles: that's how you learn by doing.
Day after day, the updates keep stacking up.
Check the board: shipped today, and more on the way.
All of that, in one day. And it keeps on shipping.
This has been the Microsoft for Education Daily.
Go build something. See you tomorrow.
